header.running_head: The Abstinence of Hadhrat Jalaaj Ghitfaani (RA)

blocks.text: to us?" "Which Hadith?" asked Hadhrat Umar (RA). Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) replied, "(The Hadith in which Rasulullaah ﷺ said,) 'The limit of a person's possessions in this world should be like the provisions of a traveller.'" "Oh yes (I have heard the Hadith)" confirmed Hadhrat Umar (RA). Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) then asked, "Now what have we done after Rasulullaah ﷺ, O Umar?" The two Sahabah (RA) then continued reminding each other (of the words of Rasulullaah ﷺ) with tears in their eyes until morning arrived.
The Abstinence of Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Afraa (RA)
The Incident with Hadhrat Umar (RA) Concerning his Attire

Hadhrat Aflah the freed slave of Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to have a set of exclusive clothing made for the veterans of Badr. When he sent such a set to Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Afraa (RA), Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) told Hadhrat Aflah to sell it. When Hadhrat Aflah sold it for one thousand five hundred Dirhams, Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) instructed him to purchase some slaves with the money. Hadhrat Afla managed to buy five slaves. Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) then said, "By Allaah! Any man who prefers wearing two sheets of cloth to setting five slaves free is certainly most foolish." He then set all the slaves free.
When Hadhrat Umar (RA) heard that Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Afraa (RA) did not wear the clothing he sent to him, he had a crude set of clothing made for him that cost a hundred Dirhams. When the messenger brought the clothing to him, Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) said, "I do not think that the Ameerul Mu'mineen had sent you to give that to me." When the messenger swore that he had been sent to him, Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) took the outfit and went to Hadhrat Umar (RA). He then asked, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Have you sent this outfit for me?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "Yes. We had sent to you an outfit that we had made for you and your brethren but subsequently heard that you did not wear it (and therefore sent you this simple clothing)." Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Even though I do not wear such clothing, I would still like to receive the best of that which you receive." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then gave him the same type of (good) clothing (as he had been giving before).[^1]
The Abstinence of Hadhrat Jalaaj Ghitfaani (RA)
His Abstinence from Eating to his Fill after Accepting Islaam
Hadhrat Jalaaj (RA) says, "Since the time I accepted Islaam at the hands of Rasulullaah ﷺ, I have never filled my belly. I eat only what is sufficient to
Umar bin Shabba, as quoted in Sifatus Safwah (Vol.1 Pg.188).
